mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while PAYEMS increases by at least 2% in the same month
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading UNRATE (p < 0.05), or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during neutral labor conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which raises expected corporate profits and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when CPIAUCSL growth is above threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% followed by a rebound of over 3% in the subsequent month suggests a supply shock, which temporarily elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline > 2% followed by > 3% increase in next month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after such an INDPRO pattern (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 1% for four consecutive months, the discount rate for future cash flows is effectively suppressed, supporting higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no correlation with FEDFUNDS level (R-squared < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates softening labor market conditions, which can trigger a short-term bearish S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases while UNRATE increases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such a labor market pattern.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signal an aggressive monetary policy stance, which can compress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate accelerates above 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when inflation accelerates (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to supply-side expansion (e.g., INDPRO > 105) combined with a sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 237) suggests capacity utilization pressures are easing, which can support positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in a recovery regime.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 105 and remains above while CPIAUCSL remains below 237 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both conditions hold (p > 0.05).
